question: In handwriting restoration, does letting a small student imitate a teacher only for character classes where the teacher showed the largest DEV advantage improve on ordinary imitation?
timing: Defined after the first ordinary-distillation pilot. Original test images are excluded from the external evaluation. No external model score used to choose the selector.
source: UCI Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits, OpenML dataset ID 28, version 1, file ID 28
external_rule: Verify last 1797 images and labels exactly match the bundled scikit-learn cohort. Require all 3823 remaining parent images to be distinct and disjoint. One fresh corruption per external parent. No external labels in training, selection or inference.
selector: Per training seed, rank the ten digit classes by mean DEV teacher-minus-vanilla PSNR. Select the top five; tie break by ascending digit. Only their training images receive weight 0.5. Labels select the loss during training only.
controls: Vanilla 240, vanilla 720, full uniform KD at 0.5, minibatch dose-matched uniform KD, randomly shuffled masks within the very same minibatch, teacher, noisy input. Same student initialization, example/noise order and update budget across 240-step arms.
decision: For every required control: positive selective-minus-control PSNR for all 3 seeds, average gain >=0.10 dB, and average gradient MAE no more than 1% worse. Teacher must beat vanilla on DEV in every seed. Long vanilla is a descriptive compute control. Report all outcomes and bootstrap intervals even on failure. Stop the pilot without retuning on this external cohort.
claim: A single class-label-based selection rule for 8x8 handwriting only. No claim about all selective distillation, other image datasets or the radar application.
